preamble: Intervocalic [j] is very prone to loss. Proto-Greek and Proto-Italic lost inherited intervocalic *y before the historical period, causing vowel contraction (*tréyes > τρεῖς, *monéyeti > moneō). Modern New Mexican and northern Mexican Spanish delete intervocalic /ʝ/ (realized as a glide) next to front vowels, and in French [j] from intervocalic g was absorbed into a preceding vowel.

examples.note: Intervocalic *y was lost and the vowels in hiatus contracted to the long vowel spelled ει.
Causative *-éye- lost its intervocalic *y in Proto-Italic (*moneō).
Conditional elision of intervocalic /ʝ/ between /i/ and a vowel, or after /e/ before /a/ or /o/; shared with northern Mexican Spanish.
The glide from lenited g merged with the preceding vowel into a diphthong, which later monophthongized.

sources: Alkire, T., & Rosen, C. (2010). Romance Languages: A Historical Introduction. Cambridge University Press.
